title: J1.2 interactive blind map teaching-examining e-learning system
description: J1.2 is a self-developed interactive blind map teaching-examining e-learning application built at the University of Debrecen on J 1.0, published as a webpage and distinguishing two user types: students and teachers. Teachers specify new exams with administrative data, a pass-mark percentage and fault tolerances in pixels, while the student interface supports exam practice and formal examinations, stores scores, and lets geographic objects stored in the database be browsed and inspected. Its database held some 181 records on nature conservation and landscape protection areas, of which 143 concern nature conservation areas and 38 landscape protection areas.
requirements: Selection requirements for development technologies included open access and capability for locating geographical objects on a blind map; presenting the attributes of selected objects; round-the-clock availability; and secure password-protected login user privilege administration facilities.
constraints: Level of difficulty is not assigned to the items; the supported browser is Mozilla Firefox.
target_learners: university bachelor and master students majoring in geography
target_learning_goals: locating named geographic entities on a blind map (topographic knowledge)
examples: Used for a course on the conservation of geoheritage, with tests placing 10 objects on a blind map under a 1 cm fault tolerance.
